Development of Mastication Monitoring System for Assessment of the Mandibular 
Asymmetry 
Y. L. Yang1, H. S. Seok2 and H. Shin1,2 
1Interdiciplanary Program of Biomedical Engineering, Chonnam National University, Gwangju , Korea 
2Department of Biomedical Engineering , Chonnam National University, Yeosu, Korea 
diddbsfk@gmail.com , shhs4695@gmail.com , hangsik.shin@jnu.ac.kr 
Abstract 
 The previous diagnostic methods of ma ndibular asymmetry are based on the still image. Therefore, it is impossible 
to analyze continuous and dynamic mastication. The purpose of this study was to develop the force sensing system 
for mastication monitoring to assess mandibular asymmetry. We developed mastication force recording system and 
evaluated its feasibility. The result shows that the developed system had high accuracy in force sensing and mastication 
activity could be recorded with developed system. 
 
Background 
Mandibular asymmetry is one of the most frequent 
dysmorphologies, but in many cases, the specific 
cause is unknown. It has be en postulated that the 
normal mandibular grows asymmetrically by human 
growing with various genetic or environmental factors 
[1]. This is the main reason of facial asymmetry, which 
leads the negative effect on one`s facial esthetics as 
well as the difficulty of mastication . Moreover, it 
could be a reason of a jaw pain, temporomandibular 
joint dysfunction or degenerative arthritis of 
mandibular [2,3]. Especially, it has been known that 
the 30% of the dysphagia that means swallowing 
disorder is originated from the difficulty of 
mastication [4]. 
Mandibular asymmetry has typically assessed by 
the two-dimensional analysis using virtual frontal 
cephalogram with a marker, the 3 -dimensional 
analysis using CT (computed tomography) or lateral 
cephalogram [5-7]. These methods are possible to 
diagnosis anatomic symmetry based on image . 
However, they have limitations in analyzing of 
continuous and dynamic jaw activity such as 
mastication. In this research, we develop ed chewing 
activity monitoring system using a force sensor for 
diagnosis mandibular asymmetry in dynamic 
condition. 
Methods 
 The purpose of this research is to develop the 
system for monitoring mastication by recording the 
force of mouth open and close . For this, we use the 
knit fabric jaw strap supporter to support and then 
measured the force between strap supporter and 
mandibular during mastication. 
2.1 System Implementation 
The proposed s ystem consists of Arduino UNO for 
processing of the signal, LCD (Nokia_5110) for 
displaying the measured force , SD card slot (NS_SD) 
and Micro SD card for data storing. We used force 
piezoresistive type force sensor, FlexiForce 
Model A201 (Tekscan co. ltd., MA, USA). 
Peripherals such as the switch and LED were also 
installed to control or debugging the system. The 
system block diagram is represented in figure 1. 
 
Figure 1. System block diagram of the proposed system 
When sensors are positioned onto the skin , it is 
impossible to measure force accurately because the 
force between the jaw supporter and the sensor could 
not be uniformly distributed over the surface of the 
sensor. Therefore, we modified the sensor structure 
with rigid and thick material. Sensor s tructure and 
implemented sensor are depicted in figure 2. Figure 2 
(a) shows the sensor structure, and figure 2 (b) and 
figure 2 (c) are the schematic of sensor interface and 
implemented sensor, respectively. 
P-111

The p roposed sensor structure consists of a force 
sensor, three silicon pads and adhesive tape; a silicon 
pad o n skin side has 19.7 mm of diameter, and two 
silicon pads o n the supporter side have 14.7 mm of 
diameter. Silicon pads make the sensor much thicker 
(~7.6 mm) and this could fill the empty space between 
mandibular and jaw supporter. Therefore, it could 
increase contact surface, which the force is delivered 
to the sensor more effectively. In experiment, we used 
5 force sensors to record the force at various locations. 
 
Figure 2. (a) Sensor structure, ( b) Developed sensor, (c) 
Sensor interface circuit 
Implemented system is represented in figure 3 . 
System cover was designed with 3D computer sided 
design program (123D Design) and was printed with 
3D printer (Replicator2, MakerBot, US) 
 
Figure 3. Developed system 
2.2 Method for system evaluation 
To convert ADC (Analog Digital to Converter) 
level which measured by Arduino UNO to actual force, 
sensor calibration is needed. We applied force using 
push and pull gauge (DS2, Imada co. ltd., Northbrook, 
IL) to each force sensor. Applied forces were 10 to 50 
N with 10 N increments, and the same test was 
repeated 5 times. Finally, conversion equations were 
derived in each channel from the average value of 
push-pull gauge experiment. 
2.3 Method for mastication monitoring 
An experiment was conducted with three participants 
(age 23 ±1 years old , height 174±6.5 cm, weight 
72±2.6 kg, 3 males) in mastication monitoring . Every 
participant has no reported mandibular disease. Figure 
4 (a) shows positioning of sensors. Sensor 3 (S3) was 
attached at midpoint of mandibular and s ensor 2 (S2), 
sensor 4 (S4) was att ached at 1 cm apart from ‘S1’ 
Sensor 1 (S1) and sensor 5 (S5) was attached on both 
sides of the angle of mandibular. Sensors were fixed 
with medical tapes, then covered with jaw strap 
supporter. Figure 4 (b) shows the appearance after 
wearing the jaw strap supporter. In the experiment, 
the alarm was given in every 3 second to notice for the 
mouth open/close. Recording is carried out for 18 
seconds. 
 
Figure 4. (a) Sensor placement location , (b) After wearing 
jaw strap supporter 
Results and Discussion 
3.1 Force measurement test 
Table 1 shows the testing result of force 
measurement. Values of table 1 are mean, standard 
deviation (SD) and standard error (SE) of measured 
force after 5 times repetition. This result suggests that 
the measured force is increased by applied force and 
average error doesn’t exceed 1 N. Figure 5 shows the 
measured force by each sensor in every trial . From the 
figure 5, we can find that the developed sensor s have 
inter-sensor difference, however, they have high 
reproducibility.

3.2 Mastication measurement 
In pilot test, significant changes were not found in 
sensor S1 and S5 . Therefore, experiment was 
performed with only sensor S3, S4 and S5. Figure 6 
shows mastication movement recorded by developed 
system. Red line of figure 6 is the requested time for 
mastication ( every 3 seconds ). There is a little time 
lags, but mastication activity could be recognized bear 
the red line.

Conclusion 
The purpose of this study was to develop the force 
sensing system for mastication monitoring to assess 
mandibular asymmetry. As a result, developed sensor 
and system show the possibility of the force sensing 
though it needs to be tested with much more number 
of subjects. In further research, it would apply to 
mandibular asymmetry patient and measure dynamic 
mastication activity data in real -time
